title: Optimising Budget Management via Primal-Dual Approximation with Constrained Polynomial Weights Update

problem.claim: Online applications need effective budget management for activities such as advertising campaigns and promotional-content allocation.

gap.claim: Existing worst-case approaches may underperform in practice, while online learning methods may lack robustness in highly non-stationary environments.

contributions.claim: An online budget pacing algorithm is developed to combine worst-case guarantees with improved average allocative efficiency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithm preserves worst-case guarantees while improving average allocative efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Budget management is important in online applications.
Prior work focuses on worst-case approximation guarantees or online learning for average performance.
Worst-case methods can perform poorly in practice, and online learning can be non-robust under strong non-stationarity.
The paper proposes an online budget pacing algorithm intended to bridge both approaches.

source_observation.claim: Worst-case guarantees and average-case performance are treated as competing priorities in budget management.

interpretation.claim: A robust system may benefit from combining formal guarantees with adaptation to typical operating conditions.

application.claim: Online allocation systems could evaluate methods on both robustness and average allocative efficiency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this tradeoff or combined approach applies beyond the described budget-management settings.

unknowns: Algorithmic details and approximation guarantees are unspecified.
Datasets, experiments, quantitative results, and baselines are unspecified.
The meaning of constrained polynomial weights update is not explained in the abstract.
